figures.caption: Fig. 1. Conceptual comparison of three retrieval views under a fixed evidence substrate. (a) Dense retrieval scores passage values independently. (b) Pairwise KG retrieval uses binary entity-relation keys and maps graph nodes back to their source passages. (c) HKVM-RAG separates key-side evidence organization from value-side passage text: an answer-path hyperedge acts as one higher-order retrieval key that maps back to multiple passage values. The schematic illustrates the mechanism tested in the cached-extraction setting.

Fig. 3. Source-effect diagnostics for dense-aware evidence control. The left panels plot ∆F1 relative to each dataset–first-stage baseline as the structured source is changed from no complement to Co-occurrence-HG, Static-HG, Weighted-KG-PPR, and WHG-KV. Colored curves denote ColBERTv2, BM25, and Contriever first-stage sources; endpoint labels mark the WHG-KV ∆F1. The right metric strip summarizes WHG-KV margins over the best non-WHG complement for F1, EM, and AR@10. These cached train-to-dev diagnostics support a WHG-KV-specific source effect, with AR@10 margins interpreted under the recall ceilings shown in Table VI.

Fig. 2. HKVM-RAG data states and dense-aware evidence control. (a) A frozen LLM evidence tuple cache stores passage-level relation triples, passage ids, and confidence fields (cf , cs, cb); it does not directly extract high-order hyperedges. (b) HKVM assembles answer-path hyperedge keys from the tuple fields, weights them with extractor confidence, diffuses query-seeded key scores, and projects the result back to passage-value scores. (c) The dense-aware controller aligns frozen ColBERTv2 and HKVM rank/score predictions by passage id and trains a passage-level logistic ranker on train-side support labels to reorder the final evidence context for the fixed answer module.
